formalStatement: let Board : ℕ → Type := fun n => Fin n → Fin n → Bool; let checkerboard : (n : ℕ) → Board n := fun n i j => decide ((i.val + j.val) % 2 = 0); let SwapOp : ℕ → Type := fun n => Bool × (Fin n × Fin n); let applyOp : (n : ℕ) → SwapOp n → Board n → Board n := fun n op b => fun r c => if op.1 then (if r = op.2.1 then b op.2.2 c else if r = op.2.2 then b op.2.1 c else b r c) else (if c = op.2.1 then b r op.2.2 else if c = op.2.2 then b r op.2.1 else b r c); let applyOps : (n : ℕ) → List (SwapOp n) → Board n → Board n := fun n ops b => List.foldl (fun b op => applyOp n op b) b ops; let Reachable : (n : ℕ) → Board n → Prop := fun n b => ∃ ops : List (SwapOp n), applyOps n ops (checkerboard n) = b; let Restoring : (n : ℕ) → Board n → ℕ → Prop := fun n b k => ∃ ops : List (SwapOp n), ops.length = k ∧ applyOps n ops b = checkerboard n; let MinCost : (n : ℕ) → Board n → ℕ → Prop := fun n b k => Restoring n b k ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, Restoring n b m → k ≤ m; let answer : ℕ → ℕ := fun n => if n % 2 = 0 then n / 2 else n - 1; ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → (∀ b : Board n, Reachable n b → ∃ k : ℕ, MinCost n b k ∧ k ≤ answer n) ∧ (∃ b : Board n, Reachable n b ∧ MinCost n b (answer n))
modelEncodingNotes: Representational encodings only: boards are Fin n -> Fin n -> Bool; the standard checkerboard is (i+j) mod 2 = 0; a swap operation is encoded as Bool × (Fin n × Fin n), with true meaning swap the two indicated rows and false meaning swap the two indicated columns; operation lists and their fold define reachability and restoration. The minimum restoration cost is expressed relationally by Restoring and MinCost instead of using sInf or Nat.find. The answer formula is encoded as n/2 for even n and n-1 for odd n, with n restricted to positive naturals.
